title: Hospital ER Director: Code Blue
description: You're the new Emergency Room Director at Mumbai Central Hospital. Lives hang in the balance every second. Manage your team, allocate scarce resources, and make impossible medical decisions under extreme time pressure. Every choice saves or costs a life.

scenes.title: First Day
scenes.narrative: It's 6 AM and you walk into Mumbai Central Hospital for your first day as ER Director. The outgoing director left suddenly — rumors say burnout. The night shift nurse hands you a clipboard full of pending cases. Your phone buzzes: 'Mass casualty alert - bus accident on Western Express Highway.'
scenes.image_prompt: Early morning at a large Indian public hospital entrance. A doctor in a white coat walks through the glass doors of Mumbai Central Hospital. Ambulance lights flash in the background. The reception area is busy with night shift staff. Warm golden sunrise light streams through the windows. Realistic, dramatic, cinematic lighting.

choices.label: Rush to the ER floor
choices.description: Head straight to the emergency room to take charge of the incoming casualties

choices.label: Review pending cases first
choices.description: Take a few minutes to understand the overnight backlog before diving in

scenes.title: The ER Floor
scenes.narrative: Chaos. Three ambulances are pulling in simultaneously. Nurses are running. A junior doctor looks to you for guidance. The triage area is overwhelmed. Stretchers line the corridor. The smell of antiseptic mixes with blood. Monitors beep frantically. This is your domain now.
scenes.image_prompt: Chaotic Indian hospital emergency room. Three ambulances visible through open bay doors. Nurses in blue scrubs running with stretchers. A young doctor looking anxious. Medical equipment and monitors everywhere. Fluorescent lighting, motion blur on running staff. Intense, documentary-style realism.

choices.label: Take charge of triage personally
choices.description: Step into the triage area yourself and start directing patient flow

choices.label: Delegate to senior staff and coordinate
choices.description: Trust your experienced team to handle triage while you coordinate the bigger picture

scenes.title: The Backlog
scenes.narrative: The clipboard reveals 15 pending cases from overnight. Equipment maintenance is overdue. Three nurses called in sick. Budget reports show overspending last quarter. The hospital is held together by duct tape and the sheer willpower of an exhausted staff. You need to pick your battles.
scenes.image_prompt: A hospital director's office cluttered with paperwork and medical files. A clipboard with a long list of cases. Budget spreadsheets on a computer screen showing red numbers. Through the office window, a busy hospital corridor is visible. Warm desk lamp lighting contrasts with harsh corridor fluorescents. Realistic, detail-rich.

choices.label: Prioritize equipment maintenance
choices.description: Get the critical medical equipment serviced before something fails during an emergency

choices.label: Focus on staff scheduling
choices.description: Reorganize the shift roster to cover the gaps and reduce burnout

scenes.title: Code Blue
scenes.narrative: The PA system crackles: 'Code Blue, Bay 4!' A patient is crashing. Your first real emergency as director. The entire ER watches to see how you handle it. A nurse is already performing CPR. The defibrillator is being wheeled in. This is your baptism by fire. Everything you do from this moment defines your leadership.
scenes.image_prompt: Intense hospital emergency scene. Medical team performing CPR on a patient in a hospital bay. A defibrillator being charged. Doctors and nurses gathered around. A new director in a white coat stepping forward decisively. Heart monitor showing flatline. Dramatic overhead lighting, high stakes atmosphere. Photorealistic, cinematic.

npcs.name: Dr. Arjun Mehta
npcs.personality: Brilliant but arrogant. 20 years of experience in trauma surgery. Resents new management and believes seniority should dictate leadership. Respects competence above all else.
npcs.domain_expertise: trauma surgery, emergency procedures, surgical protocols

npcs.name: Nurse Lakshmi Nair
npcs.personality: Compassionate, overworked, respected by everyone on the floor. Knows every corner of the hospital and every patient's name. She holds the ER together through sheer dedication.
npcs.domain_expertise: patient care, nursing operations, staff wellness, hospital logistics

npcs.name: Mr. Kapoor
npcs.personality: Budget-focused, politically connected, and always watching the bottom line. Pressures you to cut costs at every turn. Friendly on the surface but will go over your head if finances slip.
npcs.domain_expertise: hospital finance, insurance, government relations, public relations

base_rounds.title: Mass Casualty Triage
base_rounds.story: Bus accident victims flood the ER. 12 patients, 6 critical. You have 3 available trauma bays and limited blood supply. The ambulance crew is shouting vitals. Families are crowding the entrance. Your team looks to you. Who gets treated first?
base_rounds.goal: Perform triage to maximize survival with limited resources
base_rounds.image_prompt: Busy Indian hospital emergency room during a mass casualty event. Multiple stretchers with injured patients. Nurses checking vitals. Blood bags on IV stands. A triage board on the wall. Anxious family members behind a glass partition. Overhead fluorescent lights. High-intensity, photojournalistic style.
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Delayed triage! Two patients deteriorated critically while you hesitated. The ER descended into chaos without your direction.

choices.label: Prioritize most critical patients
choices.description: Focus all resources on the 6 critical patients first, stabilize them before moving to others
choices.feedback: You saved the most critical cases. Some less urgent patients had to wait, but the right call. Dr. Arjun nods approvingly — he respects decisive clinical judgment.

choices.label: Triage by chance of survival
choices.description: Use clinical assessment to treat patients with the highest survival probability first
choices.feedback: Efficient triage. Maximum lives saved with available resources. Nurse Lakshmi appreciates the systematic approach — it keeps her team organized.

choices.label: Treat on first-come basis
choices.description: Process patients in order of arrival to maintain fairness and avoid bias
choices.feedback: Fair but not optimal. Some critical patients waited too long. Families appreciate the transparency but your medical staff knows better outcomes were possible.

choices.label: Call in off-duty staff for extra capacity
choices.description: Phone off-duty doctors and nurses to come in immediately, expanding your treatment capacity
choices.feedback: All patients treated but staff is exhausted and overtime costs mount. Mr. Kapoor's phone is already buzzing with budget alerts.

base_rounds.title: The VIP Problem
base_rounds.story: A local politician arrives with chest pain. His aide demands immediate attention, bypassing the queue. Three critical patients are still waiting. The media is outside with cameras rolling. The politician's aide drops the Health Minister's name. Your staff watches to see if you bend.
base_rounds.goal: Handle VIP pressure while maintaining medical ethics
base_rounds.image_prompt: Hospital waiting area. A well-dressed politician sitting impatiently with his aide arguing with hospital staff. Other patients on stretchers in the background looking worried. TV news cameras visible through the entrance. A doctor caught in the middle. Tension visible in body language. Realistic, dramatic lighting.

choices.label: Treat based on medical priority only
choices.description: Inform the aide that all patients are treated based on clinical urgency, not status
choices.feedback: The politician's aide is furious, but your staff respects you. Nurse Lakshmi gives you a quiet nod of approval. The critical patients get treated first.

choices.label: Fast-track the politician
choices.description: Quietly move the politician ahead in the queue to avoid political complications
choices.feedback: The politician is grateful. His aide whispers about a 'generous donation.' But a nurse saw you skip the queue. Word spreads on the floor.

choices.label: Assign a dedicated team while continuing normal ops
choices.description: Split your staff — one team for the VIP, another continues treating the queue
choices.feedback: You managed both, but stretched your team thin. The nurses are running between two stations. It works, barely.

choices.label: Let Dr. Arjun handle the VIP personally
choices.description: Ask the senior surgeon to attend to the politician, satisfying both parties
choices.feedback: Dr. Arjun's ego is satisfied and the politician gets top care. A smart delegation that keeps everyone happy — for now.

base_rounds.title: Equipment Failure
base_rounds.story: The main ventilator in ICU crashes during a critical procedure. A patient is on life support. The backup is 10 years old and hasn't been tested in months. Your biomedical engineer says repair will take 2 hours minimum. The patient doesn't have 2 hours.
base_rounds.goal: Handle equipment emergency without losing patients
base_rounds.image_prompt: Hospital ICU scene. A ventilator machine with warning lights flashing red. A patient connected to life support. A biomedical engineer examining the machine with tools. Nurses looking worried. A backup ventilator — visibly old and dusty — being wheeled in. Tense, clinical atmosphere. Photorealistic, high detail.
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Equipment failure unaddressed! The patient crashed on the ventilator while you deliberated. The ICU team is shaken.

choices.label: Manual ventilation until repair
choices.description: Have nurses hand-ventilate the patient using a bag valve mask until the machine is fixed
choices.feedback: Nurses take turns hand-ventilating for two grueling hours. Exhausting but effective. The patient stabilizes. Your nursing team is spent.

choices.label: Transfer patient to nearby hospital
choices.description: Arrange emergency ambulance transfer to Lilavati Hospital across the city
choices.feedback: Risky transfer, but successful. Media questions why Mumbai Central can't handle its own patients. The ambulance ride was touch-and-go.

choices.label: Deploy the backup ventilator
choices.description: Power up the old backup ventilator and hope it holds together
choices.feedback: The old backup ventilator whirs to life. Will it hold? Everyone watches the monitors anxiously...

choices.label: Emergency purchase authorization
choices.description: Authorize an immediate purchase of a new ventilator from a medical supplier across town
choices.feedback: Expensive but you got a new ventilator delivered within the hour. The patient is saved. Mr. Kapoor will have a heart attack when he sees the bill.

base_rounds.title: The Night Shift Crisis
base_rounds.story: Night shift. Half your staff called in sick — monsoon flu is sweeping through Mumbai. The ER is packed wall to wall. A trauma case, two cardiac emergencies, and a pediatric patient all arrive within 15 minutes. The skeleton crew looks at you with exhausted eyes. The hospital feels like a sinking ship.
base_rounds.goal: Manage extreme understaffing during peak emergency hours
base_rounds.image_prompt: Night scene inside a dimly lit Indian hospital ER. Rain visible through windows. Exhausted medical staff in scrubs with dark circles under their eyes. Multiple patients on stretchers in the corridor. A child on a gurney with a worried mother. Clock on the wall showing 2 AM. Moody, atmospheric lighting. Cinematic realism.

choices.label: Personally work the floor
choices.description: Roll up your sleeves, put on gloves, and work alongside your team through the night
choices.feedback: Your team sees you in the trenches — suturing wounds, checking vitals, comforting patients. Morale soars. You haven't slept in 20 hours but neither has anyone else.

choices.label: Activate mutual aid with nearby hospitals
choices.description: Call neighboring hospitals to send backup staff and accept patient transfers
choices.feedback: Other hospitals send support. Collaborative approach works. Staff from Hinduja and KEM arrive within the hour. Mumbai's medical community sticks together.

choices.label: Implement strict triage — turn away non-emergencies
choices.description: Redirect all non-life-threatening cases to clinics and other hospitals
choices.feedback: Tough call. Some patients were turned away in the rain. A local news channel captures footage. Social media erupts. But your critical patients all survived.

choices.label: Keep skeleton staff, focus on critical cases
choices.description: Work with minimal staff and pray that no more emergencies come in
choices.feedback: Risky gamble with minimal staff. You hold your breath every time the ambulance siren wails outside...

base_rounds.title: Pandemic Preparedness

ai_generation_context.context: Mid-game challenge during ER management at Mumbai Central Hospital. The player is the ER Director facing a potential disease outbreak or infection control scenario based on their earlier decisions.

base_rounds.image_prompt: a bustling city health center with staff in scrubs preparing vaccines, bright fluorescent lights illuminating the room, a sense of urgency and hope in the air

base_rounds.title: The Budget Showdown
base_rounds.story: Hospital board meeting. Mr. Kapoor presents the quarterly numbers — you're ₹20 Lakhs over budget. The board chairman taps his pen impatiently. Department heads are nervous. The board wants cuts. Where do you compromise? Your medical ethics and financial reality are about to collide.
base_rounds.goal: Navigate budget politics while protecting patient care
base_rounds.image_prompt: Corporate boardroom in an Indian hospital. Long polished table with board members in formal attire. A projector screen showing financial charts with red downward arrows. A hospital administrator presenting budget numbers. The ER director sitting across, looking determined. Tense corporate atmosphere. Realistic, professional lighting.

choices.label: Cut administrative overhead
choices.description: Propose reducing administrative staff, paperwork duplication, and executive perks
choices.feedback: Smart cuts. Admin staff grumbles but medical staff cheers. Mr. Kapoor takes it personally — you just cut his department.

choices.label: Reduce non-essential equipment spending
choices.description: Delay planned equipment upgrades and extend maintenance cycles
choices.feedback: Budget saved, but some equipment gets older. The biomedical engineer warns that deferred maintenance always costs more in the long run.

choices.label: Propose a fundraising campaign
choices.description: Launch a community fundraising drive and approach corporate CSR funds
choices.feedback: Community responds warmly. Local businesses contribute. A Tata Trust CSR grant comes through. Donations start flowing in.

choices.label: Present data on how investment saves money long-term
choices.description: Show the board an ROI analysis proving that spending on care reduces costly complications
choices.feedback: Your ROI analysis convinces some board members. The data is compelling — preventing readmissions saves more than cutting budgets. A few members applaud.

base_rounds.title: The Ethical Dilemma
base_rounds.story: A 12-year-old girl needs an emergency transplant. A matching organ just arrived. But there's a 45-year-old father of three on the list who's been waiting longer. Hospital policy says first-come-first-served. The transplant coordinator looks at you. Both families are praying in the hallway. Your call.
base_rounds.goal: Make an impossible ethical decision under time pressure
base_rounds.image_prompt: Hospital corridor with two families on opposite sides. On one side, parents holding a sick child's hand. On the other, a wife and three young children waiting anxiously. A doctor in the middle holding a medical file, looking torn. Organ transport cooler visible in the background. Emotional, soft lighting. Deeply human, photorealistic.
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: You couldn't decide! Both patients' conditions worsened while you deliberated. The transplant window is closing. Your team is shaken by the indecision.

choices.label: Follow the waitlist — give it to the father
choices.description: Honor the established protocol. The father has waited longer and the rules must apply equally
choices.feedback: Following protocol. The child's family is devastated but the system was fair. Your staff respects the consistency. The transplant is successful.

choices.label: Prioritize the child — youth takes precedence
choices.description: The child has more years of life ahead. Make the difficult call to prioritize her
choices.feedback: The child survives. The father's family threatens legal action. The ethics committee will want a review. Dr. Arjun quietly tells you he would have done the same.

choices.label: Consult the ethics committee
choices.description: Convene an emergency ethics review to make the decision collectively
choices.feedback: The committee deliberates and reaches a consensus. A measured approach, though time-consuming. Both families feel heard. The process, while slow, protects the institution.

choices.label: Check if organ can be split for both
choices.description: Consult with the transplant surgeon about the possibility of splitting the organ for both patients
choices.feedback: An unconventional approach. The transplant surgeon raises an eyebrow. High risk, potentially high reward. The entire OR holds its breath...

base_rounds.title: The Aftermath
base_rounds.story: Three months into your tenure. The hospital's performance metrics are being reviewed. Your decisions have shaped the ER into what it is today. The board, staff, and community all have opinions. Now you must choose your legacy — what will define Mumbai Central Hospital going forward?
base_rounds.goal: Reflect on your leadership and plan for the future
base_rounds.image_prompt: A hospital director standing at a window overlooking Mumbai's skyline at sunset. Behind them, a wall covered with performance charts, patient thank-you letters, newspaper clippings, and team photos. A desk with a steaming cup of chai. Warm golden hour light. Reflective, hopeful mood. Cinematic, wide angle.

choices.label: Implement a comprehensive training program
choices.description: Invest in continuous medical education, simulation training, and skill development for all staff
choices.feedback: Long-term investment in your team's skills. Monthly simulation drills begin. Junior doctors gain confidence. The ER becomes a teaching hospital.

choices.label: Launch a community health initiative
choices.description: Start outreach programs in nearby slums to prevent emergencies before they happen
choices.feedback: Preventing emergencies is better than treating them. Health camps in Dharavi and Kurla reduce ER admissions by 15%. The community embraces you.

choices.label: Push for technology upgrades
choices.description: Invest in modern monitoring systems, digital records, and AI-assisted diagnostics
choices.feedback: State-of-the-art equipment transforms your ER. AI triage assistance, real-time monitoring dashboards, and electronic health records modernize the entire department.

choices.label: Focus on staff wellness and retention
choices.description: Create a wellness program with counseling, reasonable shifts, and career growth paths
choices.feedback: Happy staff means better patient care. Staff turnover drops 40%. A wellness room is set up. Nurse Lakshmi says it's the first time she's felt valued in years.

crisis_events.title: Mass Food Poisoning
crisis_events.description: 50 students from a nearby municipal school arrive with severe food poisoning. Vomiting, dehydration, and panic. Parents are flooding the entrance. Your ER is already at capacity from the bus accident aftermath. The school principal is hysterical.
crisis_events.image_prompt: Overwhelmed hospital entrance with dozens of school children in uniforms being brought in by teachers and parents. Some children on stretchers, others sitting on the floor looking sick. Ambulances and auto-rickshaws parked haphazardly. Chaotic, urgent atmosphere. Photojournalistic realism.

choices.label: Set up triage tents outside
choices.description: Deploy emergency tents in the hospital parking area to expand capacity
choices.feedback: Triage tents go up in 20 minutes. Your team divides efficiently between indoor and outdoor stations. All 50 students are treated. Parents are relieved and grateful.

choices.label: Redirect to other hospitals
choices.description: Send half the students to nearby hospitals to distribute the load
choices.feedback: Some students are redirected but a few dehydrated children deteriorate during transport. Parents question why Mumbai Central turned away sick children.

crisis_events.title: Power Outage
crisis_events.description: A massive thunderstorm knocks out hospital power. Generators kick in but only cover the ICU. The ER goes dark. Monitors shut off. Emergency lighting casts eerie shadows. Three patients are mid-procedure. The backup generator has enough fuel for 4 hours.
crisis_events.image_prompt: Dark hospital emergency room lit only by emergency red lights and flashlights held by nurses. Medical equipment screens are black. Rain lashing against windows. A doctor performing a procedure by flashlight. Eerie, tense atmosphere. Dramatic chiaroscuro lighting. Cinematic.

choices.label: Activate emergency lighting protocol
choices.description: Use portable lights, phone flashlights, and battery-powered equipment to continue ER operations
choices.feedback: The ER operates by flashlight and portable lamps. It's primitive but functional. Nurse Lakshmi produces emergency lanterns she'd stored for exactly this scenario.

choices.label: Move critical patients to ICU
choices.description: Transfer all critical ER patients to the ICU where generators are running
choices.feedback: Critical patients are moved safely. The ICU is now overcrowded but powered. Staff are exhausted from carrying patients through dark corridors.

crisis_events.title: Staff Walkout Threat
crisis_events.description: Junior doctors threaten a walkout over 36-hour shifts. The Maharashtra Association of Resident Doctors (MARD) union representative arrives at your office. They have a list of demands. The media has been tipped off. If they walk, the ER collapses.
crisis_events.image_prompt: Hospital corridor with a group of young doctors in white coats holding a meeting. Some look angry, others exhausted. A union representative with papers in hand confronting the ER director. Other staff watching nervously from doorways. Tense standoff atmosphere. Documentary-style realism.

choices.label: Negotiate immediate concessions
choices.description: Offer reduced shift hours, better on-call rooms, and overtime pay effective immediately
choices.feedback: The junior doctors stand down. New shift limits of 24 hours are implemented. The on-call room gets proper beds. It costs money but the ER stays open.

choices.label: Appeal to their duty and promise future changes
choices.description: Remind them of the patients who depend on them and commit to a reform committee
choices.feedback: Your heartfelt appeal works — barely. The doctors agree to a 30-day grace period. But the clock is ticking on your promises. They won't wait forever.

crisis_events.title: Celebrity Patient Media Frenzy
crisis_events.description: A Bollywood celebrity is rushed in from a film set accident in Film City. Paparazzi swarm the entrance. Media vans block the ambulance bay. Fans gather outside. Your ER is turning into a circus. Real patients can't get through. The celebrity's manager demands a private wing.
crisis_events.image_prompt: Hospital entrance swarmed by paparazzi with cameras and flash photography. Media vans with satellite dishes blocking the driveway. Security guards trying to maintain order. Fans holding signs. An ambulance stuck behind the media vehicles. Chaotic, circus-like atmosphere. Photojournalistic style.

choices.label: Lock down the ER, media blackout
choices.description: Clear the ambulance bay, ban all non-medical visitors, and issue a no-comment order
choices.feedback: The lockdown restores order. Ambulances can access the bay again. The celebrity gets proper treatment. Media grumbles but the public respects your priorities.

choices.label: Give a brief press statement to manage the crowd
choices.description: Hold a quick press briefing to satisfy the media and disperse the crowd peacefully
choices.feedback: Your composed 2-minute statement goes viral. 'Patient privacy is sacred at Mumbai Central.' The media disperses. But the time you spent on PR was time away from patients.

interdependencies.message: Burnt-out staff is making critical errors! Medication mistakes and delayed responses are increasing.

achievements.title: Zero Casualties
achievements.description: Achieve a patient survival rate of 95% or higher. A near-perfect record of saving lives.

achievements.title: Team Leader
achievements.description: Build staff morale to 85 or above. Your team would follow you anywhere.

achievements.title: Budget Master
achievements.description: Maintain a hospital budget of ₹60,000K or above. Financially responsible leadership.

achievements.title: People's Doctor
achievements.description: Earn public trust of 80 or above. The community believes in your hospital.

achievements.title: Equipment Excellence
achievements.description: Maintain equipment status at 80 or above. A well-oiled medical machine.

achievements.title: ER Veteran
achievements.description: Complete the game with a survival rate of 50% or above. You survived the trenches.

endings.title: Medical Legend 🏥
endings.message: Under your leadership, Mumbai Central became the gold standard for emergency medicine in India. Medical journals feature your protocols. Lives saved: countless. The National Medical Commission invites you to help draft new ER guidelines for the entire country.

endings.title: Respected Director 👨‍⚕️
endings.message: You earned the respect of your team and community. The ER runs smoothly and efficiently. Not perfect, but damn good. Patients request Mumbai Central by name. Your resignation offers pile up — everyone wants you — but you stay.

endings.title: Budget Hero 💰
endings.message: You kept the lights on and the budget balanced. The board loves you. Some say you cared more about numbers than patients, but the hospital survived when others didn't. Mr. Kapoor nominates you for the Healthcare Finance Leadership Award.

endings.title: Overwhelmed 😰
endings.message: The ER was too much. Staff turnover, budget issues, and declining outcomes. You did your best, but sometimes the system wins. You leave with hard-earned lessons and a deep respect for everyone who stays in the trenches.

endings.title: Burnout 🔥
endings.message: You gave everything to the hospital — including your own health. Your resignation letter cites 'personal reasons' but everyone knows the real cost. Nurse Lakshmi hugs you on your last day. 'Take care of yourself, Doctor. You forgot to do that.'

random_events.title: Blood Shortage
random_events.description: The blood bank reports critically low stocks of O-negative and B-positive blood types. Elective surgeries may need to be postponed. The shortage affects emergency transfusions.

random_events.title: Volunteer Surge
random_events.description: A group of medical college students and NGO volunteers arrives at the hospital offering to help. Their enthusiasm is infectious and they take on administrative tasks, freeing up your medical staff.

transfer_exercises.real_world: Competing for market share in a business with a tight budget
transfer_exercises.challenge: Identify a competitive situation in your life. What is your unique advantage?

transfer_exercises.game_context: Choosing between safe and bold strategies against AI
transfer_exercises.real_world: Deciding when to challenge the status quo versus play it safe
transfer_exercises.challenge: Research one company that made a bold risk that paid off. What conditions made it possible?

glossary_terms.definition: Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement — your fallback if no deal is reached.
glossary_terms.example: If you can't agree on a price, you could sell to a different buyer — that's your BATNA.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: A strong BATNA gives negotiating power. Knowing both parties' BATNAs reveals who needs the deal more.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: A job applicant with another offer has a stronger BATNA and can negotiate more confidently.

glossary_terms.definition: Finding solutions where both parties gain value rather than one side winning at the other's expense.
glossary_terms.example: Agreeing on a payment plan that works for both buyer and seller, rather than a discount that hurts profit.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Integrative negotiation expands the 'pie' by identifying trade-offs where each party values things differently.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Labor-management negotiations that increase productivity in exchange for better wages can benefit both sides.

glossary_terms.definition: Setting an initial reference point in a negotiation that influences the final outcome.
glossary_terms.example: The first price mentioned in a negotiation becomes the anchor around which all counteroffers are compared.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research shows people are heavily influenced by the first number they hear, even when irrelevant.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Salary negotiations: starting with a high number tends to result in higher final offers.

coaching_moment: You're the new Emergency Room Director at Mumbai Central Hospital. Lives hang in the balance every second.
cultural_context: India's doctor-to-patient ratio is among the lowest in the world at 0.7 per 1,000, creating immense pressure on hospital administrators. This game builds the triage thinking and resource-allocation skills needed by India's future healthcare leaders.
reflection_prompt: How did you adapt as the AI shifted strategies? Which adaptation worked best?
